blocking_findings.finding: The revised P-4 protocol is internally impossible. Each latency sample waits through the last visible renderSettle(completed), so the next zoom commit has no in-flight render to cancel. Nevertheless, task .6 requires renderCancel to precede the new renderStart on every commit. A correctly implemented renderer may therefore fail the acceptance criterion precisely because the preceding render already completed.
blocking_findings.required_change: Separate the measurements: retain 20 sequential commit-to-settle samples for p95 latency, but add a distinct deliberately-overlapped zoom/fit sequence that commits again while rendering is demonstrably in flight and asserts cancel → cancelled settle → replacement renderStart ordering. Do not require a cancellation for commits made after prior work settled.

blocking_findings.finding: The plan assumes that fulfilling cMap and standard-font requests with 404 will produce the same classified document-load bootstrap failure as a worker failure. PDF.js can treat missing auxiliary cMap/font data as page-render warnings or degraded output rather than rejecting getDocument, while the proposed classifier and fallback flow only consume document-load errors. Thus the required cMap/font fallback screenshots and notices are not guaranteed to be reachable through the specified architecture.
blocking_findings.required_change: Define an executable error propagation contract for auxiliary-asset failures, including whether page-render failures are surfaced from use-pdf-pages to PdfViewer and classified as bootstrap errors. Add deterministic tests for that path. Alternatively limit the R8 bootstrap-state proof to worker bootstrap failure, as R18 already states, and test cMap/font 404 behavior according to PDF.js's observed semantics without requiring an unsupported fallback transition.

blocking_findings.finding: The canonical spec JSON names branch `fn-112-native-pdfjs-document-renderer`, while the user-specified and actual current branch is `feat/native-pdf-renderer`. This is unresolved repository-metadata inconsistency under a gate that explicitly requires MD/JSON consistency and implementation from the current artifacts.
blocking_findings.required_change: Reconcile `branch_name` with the authorized current branch, or explicitly document why Flow-Next branch metadata intentionally differs and prove the implementation workflow will not create or target the wrong branch.

non_blocking_observations.observation: The baseline ordering is now executable because task .2 has no dependencies and records the baseline before dependency/product changes. Preserve the baseline artifacts independently of later task cleanup.

The existing endpoint resolves a relative asset path from dirname(recordSourcePath ?? relPath), so a basename is the natural self-PDF path. The demanded nested/container/recordSourcePath and same-basename tests appropriately prevent this from remaining an assumption.

P8 is appropriately reconciled with the user's explicit single-repository/no-publication authorization: in-repo documentation and a mechanical hosted-site handoff brief are required, while gno.sh mutation, QA, deployment, push, PR, and publication are excluded.

coverage_summary: P1, P2, P3, P6, P7 and observations N1-N7 are materially incorporated: the facade contract is coherent; dependency order is executable; genuine font/cMap fixtures and behavioral offline proof are required; StrictMode and stale-load races are precise; fallback state is DocView-owned; Range/realpath, CSP/framing, safe-link/no-scripting, accessibility, asset derivation, installed-package smoke, and frontend-design gating are covered. P4/P5 are not fully resolved because the P-4 cancellation protocol is contradictory and auxiliary cMap/font failure states lack a guaranteed propagation path. The spec JSON also disagrees with the active branch. Canonical Grok 4.5 must not begin implementation from these artifacts.
